policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere מוּסְד֤וֹת and ketiv מיסדות are orthographic variants of the same plural noun 'foundations'; both yield ASV 'the foundations of the side-chambers'. The verse's mapped notes are both classed alternative_rendering (English wording of 'raised basement' and 'of six cubits to the joining') plus a hebrew_gloss, none of which is a textual note, so nothing in the ASV distinguishes the readings. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

Qere וְאַתִּיקֶ֛יהָא and ketiv ואתוקיהא differ only in the vowel letter of the same noun 'galleries'; both underlie ASV 'and the galleries thereof on the one side and on the other side'. The verse carries no mapped textual note, so the English cannot distinguish them. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
